messages.subject: Coding Encounter Data File (EDF)
messages.body_plain:
Dear oSCR team,

Im Victor again. I have a question about data entry for oSCR (Encounter Data File, EDF)

This is my question: How to code that an animal was detected multiple times during the same sample occasion and in the same trap?.

In the toy example below, the same animal (ID=1) was detected 5 times (rows in red) during the same occasion (Sample Occasion =3) and in the same trap (TrapID = 51).

In my data, I can measure how many times an animal visit a trap during 1 day (1 day of measurement is my unit of sample occasion)

This data entry is OK for oSCR?

Session ID Occasion trapID

1,]1 1 1  21

[3,] 1 1 3 51

[4,] 1 1 3 51

[5,] 1 1 3 51

[6,] 1 1 3 51

[7,] 1 1 3 51

[8,]1 1 4 51

How to code this type of encounter data?.

Thanks in advance!

Victor

messages.subject: RE: Coding Encounter Data File (EDF)
messages.body_plain:
Hi Victor,

Yes, indeed. You simply provide a row for each observation and if individuals were observed in the same trap and in the same occasion multiple times you would end up with replicate rows. Couple of things:

1.       data2oscr() allows you to set all x>1 values to 0 or retain the frequencies. Specifically, the argument ‘remove.extracaps =’ does this if set to TRUE (which is the default). If set to FALSE, the counts are left as is.

2.       If you keep the counts you will also need to specify this when fitting models. For example, the binomial model (encmod = “B”) is the choice for binary encounter data, while the Poisson model (encmod = “P”) is the choice if you have frequencies.

3.       The interpretation of p0 (which, in hindsight should be called more generally, g0) depends on the encounter model chosen.

Chris

messages.subject: Re: Coding Encounter Data File (EDF)
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

Thanks, so now I know that my data format is fine, and I just should use ‘remove.extracaps to TRUE’  for running the  binomial model (using encmod = “B”), OR set ‘remove.extracaps to FALSE"  in order to run the Poisson model (using encmod = “P”).

Thanks again!

Best!!!!!

Victor
